Units digit: 11^3 ends in 1, 3x^2=363 ends in 3, 3x=33 ends in 3, so 1-3+3-1 ends in 0; only 1000 ends in 0. Also magnitude: value < x^3=1331 since 3x^2>3x, killing 1694 and 1331.

items.note: Expression is (x-1)^3 = 10^3 = 1000. Units-digit check alone decides the item without the binomial recognition.
(x+3)(x+4) at x=6 gives 9 by 10, perimeter 38. 90 is the area lure; 40/42 are off-by-one side lures. No shortcut kills an option without factoring/dividing.

free_elimination.how: Adjacency: stem asks for least integer meeting a threshold and the set contains exactly one adjacent pair (33, 34), so the answer is the ceiling and one of that pair

items.note: 5n/12 >= 14 gives n >= 33.6, least whole number 34. 33 is the round-down lure.

free_elimination.how: Triangle inequality: diagonal < length + width = half the perimeter = 28; 40, 28 and 192 all fail. Only 20 survives without using the ratio.

items.note: Bisectors of a linear pair always meet at 90 (35+55). 70 and 35 are given-number lures; well-known fact.

free_elimination.how: A difference of probabilities is at most 1, killing 3; experimental is at most 1 and theoretical is 0.5, so the excess is at most 0.5, killing 0.56

items.note: 28/50 = 0.56, minus 0.5 = 0.06. 3 is the count excess (28-25); 0.28 a halving lure.

free_elimination.how: Symmetry/magnitude: the median of an evenly spaced list from 2 to 100 sits near the middle (about 50), killing 2 and 25; parity: an even-count list's median is the mean of two consecutive evens, which is odd, killing 52

items.note: (50+52)/2 = 51. All three distractors die from range plus parity without computing.

free_elimination.how: Denominator: there are 90 two-digit numbers, so the reduced denominator must divide 90, killing 1/11; repdigits use a single digit 1-9, so at most 9 qualify, killing 11/90

items.note: 9 repdigits of 90 numbers = 1/10. 1/9 is the 9-of-81 or wrong-denominator lure.

free_elimination.how: Bracket from printed limits: fewer than 100 pencils and pens, so packs < 100/6 + 100/8, about 29.2; 32 dies

items.note: Equal counts are a multiple of LCM 24 under 100: 96. 16 + 12 = 28 packs. 16 is pencil packs alone; 21 from n=72.

free_elimination.how: Divisibility read off stem: 90 is not a multiple of 8; 720 = 8*90 is a multiple of 90, so gcd(720,90) = 90, not 30

items.note: n must be a multiple of lcm(8,30)=120 and gcd(120,90)=30. 240 also satisfies the conditions but is not least.
